description: Release wait: docs/adr/0019-renovate-release-wait.md. No hourly limit, so a pin bump never waits behind others.

ubuntu-snapshot.description: The Ubuntu archive snapshot the core image's apt uses (docs/adr/0022-all-inputs-are-pinned.md). The snapshot service lists no snapshots and takes any timestamp, so the latest is the day the security pocket last changed, read from its InRelease Date line: at most one bump a day. The suite is the codename of the core image's Ubuntu release: change it with that release

customManagers.description: <NAME>_VERSION pins below a `# renovate:` comment in Dockerfiles and smoke scripts
Quoted attribute pins below a `# renovate:` comment in the Coder template

packageRules.description: Docker's packages are looked up in the apt repository the core image installs them from, which publishes a release hours or days after GitHub does, so Renovate proposes only versions that install. The suite is the codename of the core image's Ubuntu release: change it with that release. The apt repository publishes no release timestamps, so these updates go ahead without the release wait rather than being held forever
The Ubuntu snapshot bumps with no release wait: it carries security fixes, and Ubuntu's updates have already passed its own -proposed testing
An x.y.0 release waits longer than the default, since those usually carry the most bugs
Child Dockerfiles default BASE_IMAGE to our own image for plain local builds; CI always builds them on this commit's parent. Never pin or bump it.

Digests of our own images (.devcontainer.json, the Coder template): one grouped pull request as soon as edge moves, with no release wait (GHCR publishes no release timestamps, and CI already built and tested edge).
